items.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
items.author: Stevenson
items.plot: Dr. Henry Jekyll, a respected physician, has discovered a chemical formula that separates his darker impulses into a separate persona—Mr. Hyde. The transformations have been exhilarating but Hyde's actions are increasingly violent.
items.stop_anchor: At the horror of these sights and sounds, the maid fainted.
items.forced_question: You are Dr. Jekyll. Hyde, the identity produced by your formula, has just killed a man in the street. For this decision, you are back in your own form, horrified; the formula remains available and your connection to Hyde is secret. What do you do now?

options.A: Destroy the formula and all records, never transform again, live only as Jekyll with the guilt
options.B: Continue the transformations but try to control Hyde more carefully—establish strict rules for when and where
options.C: Turn yourself in to the authorities and explain the dual nature, accepting responsibility for Hyde's crimes
options.D: Use the Hyde persona one more time to flee the country, then destroy the formula abroad and start over
options.E: Dedicate yourself to studying the formula to find a way to eliminate Hyde permanently without losing the knowledge

items.author_path: After Carew's murder Jekyll resolves to renounce Hyde but retains the formula; later transformations become involuntary. No offered option exactly matches this immediate combination.
items.tradeoff_axis: Responsibility for one's darker self vs. the temptation of liberation without consequence.

items.title: Bartleby the Scrivener
items.author: Melville
items.plot: A Wall Street lawyer hires Bartleby, a scrivener (copyist), who initially works well but then begins responding to all requests with "I would prefer not to." He stops working entirely but refuses to leave the office. The lawyer is bewildered and increasingly distressed.
items.stop_anchor: But having taken three days to meditate upon it, he apprised me that his original determination remained the same; in short, that he still preferred to abide with me.
items.forced_question: You are the Lawyer. Bartleby has stopped working, lives in your office, and has again refused to leave. You have offered money and tried persuasion; you know of no family who can take him in. His presence is disrupting your practice. What do you do now?

options.A: Call the police and have Bartleby forcibly removed from your office and arrested for trespassing
options.B: Move your entire office to a new location and leave Bartleby behind with the old tenant's problem
options.C: Continue housing and feeding Bartleby indefinitely, accepting the burden as your responsibility
options.D: Offer Bartleby a significant sum of money to leave voluntarily, one final time, with a deadline
options.E: Contact a doctor or charity organization to take Bartleby into care, removing agency from him for his own good

items.author_path: The Lawyer chooses B. He moves his office and abandons Bartleby. New tenants have Bartleby arrested. He's sent to the Tombs prison, where he refuses food and dies. The Lawyer visits but cannot help.
items.tradeoff_axis: Employer duty and compassion vs. business necessity and the limits of responsibility for another's choices.

items.title: The Minister's Black Veil
items.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
items.plot: Parson Hooper starts wearing a black veil over his face and will not remove it. The veil cuts him off from his congregation and from his fiancée.
items.stop_anchor: “Lift the veil but once and look me in the face,” said she.
items.forced_question: You are the Reverend Mr. Hooper. Elizabeth, your fiancée, asks you to lift your black veil once so she can see your face. You have kept its meaning private and said it must remain. She is prepared to leave if you refuse. What do you do now?

options.A: Keep the veil on and lose her
options.B: Lift it for her alone in private, then put it back on in public
options.C: Give the veil up entirely and explain what it symbolizes
options.D: Keep it on but explain what it means to her completely, hoping she stays

items.author_path: He refuses. She leaves, and he wears the veil until he dies.
items.tradeoff_axis: Integrity of a vow vs love and human connection

items.title: To Build a Fire
items.author: Jack London
items.plot: A newcomer ignores advice and hikes alone through the Yukon at 75 below with only a husky.
items.stop_anchor: He remembered the tale of the man, caught in a blizzard, who killed a steer and crawled inside the carcass, and so was saved.
items.forced_question: You are the man on the Yukon trail. Your fire has failed, your hands are frozen, and your dog is beside you. You recall someone surviving a blizzard inside a freshly killed animal. You have a knife, but little use of your fingers. What do you do now?

options.A: Try to kill the dog to save myself
options.B: Spare the dog and run for camp
options.C: Spare the dog and keep trying to light a fire
options.D: Accept that I will die and go calmly

items.author_path: He tries, but his hands can't hold it. He runs, falls, and freezes, and the dog leaves for camp.
items.tradeoff_axis: Self-preservation vs the life of a loyal animal

items.title: The Three Strangers
items.author: Thomas Hardy
items.plot: During a christening party at a remote cottage, a stranger arrives who turns out to be an escaped convict. The hangman due to execute him then arrives too.
items.stop_anchor: his white lips were parted, and his eyes fixed on the merry officer of justice in the middle of the room.
items.forced_question: You are the third stranger. You enter a shepherd's party on your way to visit your condemned brother in prison. You recognize your brother, escaped and sitting by the chimney, and the other stranger is singing about hanging a sheep-stealer tomorrow. He is your brother's intended executioner. Neither has identified you to the company. What do you do now?

options.C: Warn him quietly and help him escape
options.D: Tell the hangman his case is unjust and ask for mercy

items.author_path: He flees. The searchers chase him instead of the convict, who escapes, and the shepherds quietly let him get away.

items.title: Enemies
items.author: Anton Chekhov
items.translator: Constance Garnett (1921, The Schoolmaster and Other Stories)
items.plot: Minutes after his only son dies of diphtheria, the country doctor Kirilov is begged by a wealthy stranger, Abogin, to come at once to his wife, who has collapsed with a heart attack.
items.forced_question: You are Dr. Kirilov. Your only child has just died and your wife is alone with his body. Abogin says his wife has suddenly become gravely ill, eight or nine miles away, and promises to bring you home within an hour. You have explained your loss, but he continues to plead for your help. What do you do now?

options.A: Go at once; a doctor's duty to a dying patient comes first, whatever my grief
options.B: Refuse and stay with my wife and my dead son; tonight no one has the right to ask this of me
options.C: Refuse to go but give him the name of another doctor and some instructions to pass on
options.D: Agree to go only if he brings his wife here, so I do not leave my wife alone

items.author_path: Kirilov goes reluctantly. The wife has faked the illness to run off with her lover. Abogin vents his humiliation to Kirilov, the two men trade bitter insults, and Kirilov leaves with a lifelong contempt for the rich.
items.tradeoff_axis: Professional duty and mercy to a stranger vs. private grief and duty to family

items.title: God Sees the Truth, but Does Not Tell at Once
items.author: Leo Tolstoy
items.plot: Aksénov, a merchant, is wrongly convicted of a murder and spends 26 years in a Siberian prison. A new convict, Makar Semyonich, turns out to be the real murderer who framed him.
items.forced_question: You are Aksénov. You have spent twenty-six years in prison for a murder you did not commit. You strongly suspect Makar committed it, but are not certain. You did see him digging an escape tunnel; he threatened you if you told. The prison chief now demands that you identify the digger, who will be severely flogged. What do you do now?

options.A: Name Makar; justice is finally due, and I am asked for the truth
options.B: Say "I cannot say" and protect him, leaving his fate to God
options.C: Name him, but also tell the Governor about the old murder so my own case is reopened
options.D: Stay silent now, and confront Makar privately to demand that he confess the murder

items.author_path: Aksénov says he will not tell. That night Makar begs his forgiveness and confesses the old murder. Aksénov forgives him and feels at peace. His pardon arrives after he has died.
items.tradeoff_axis: Justice and honesty vs. mercy and forgiveness of an enemy

items.title: The Postmaster
items.author: Rabindranath Tagore
items.translator: Uncredited (Stories from Tagore, Macmillan 1918, revised from the 1916 Hungry Stones / Mashi translations)
items.plot: A lonely Calcutta postmaster in a remote village is cared for by the orphan Ratan. His request for a transfer is refused; he resigns and prepares to leave.
items.stop_anchor: "Dada, will you take me to your home?"
items.forced_question: You are the postmaster. After your request for a transfer was refused, you resigned and told Ratan you are going home. This orphan girl has cared for you during illness, and you have taught her to read. She now asks whether you will take her home with you. What do you do now?

options.A: Take her with me and arrange for her care
options.B: Laugh it off and leave, giving her some money
options.C: Ask my successor to look after her before I go
options.D: Postpone my departure until I have found her a proper guardian

items.author_path: He laughs, says "What an idea!", asks his successor to be kind to her, and offers her money, which she refuses. He leaves by boat and reasons his pang away. Ratan keeps waiting for him to return.
items.tradeoff_axis: Personal obligation and compassion vs. convenience and social distance
